body.text: Reporter: God, only now do I feel how terrifying dxm's rewriting of cognition is. Before March I o'd only occasionally, only when the pain was truly unbearable.

Reporter: then in March I tried raising the dose, roughly up to the fourth plateau. My vision seemed frame-locked, maybe changing once a second; a few seconds later everything went black for a moment; I was talking nonsense and crying; in the end, with the last of my awareness, I had my guardian feed me lorazepam and shut down.

Reporter: after that I o'd wildly with no awareness of it, or no control over it. All through March the records show twenty times: dextro, prega, Stilnox. Looking at it now I can't believe I could use at that rate. Then in April I got gastroenteritis and threw up everything I ate, which calmed me down a bit; plus magnesium L-threonate, and I recovered somewhat from that long dissociation.

Reporter: right at the start of May dextro moved to Schedule II, and I thought I'd quit along with it. Then a few days ago I thought, one last o, and while high I very unreasonably bought twenty more boxes, taking the risk. Now, seeing what's written on the wiki, I realise: it was the dextro that took my judgment, and that kept me from noticing.
Reporter: what am I supposed to do 😭
Reporter: today a police car parked at the entrance to the compound, and I instinctively assumed it was here for me (a bit of persecutory delusion, I know).
Gotō: Absolutely — because the problem is exactly in the cognition.
Gotō: you have to recognise what's left of your life besides Umi.
Gotō: why not defect to the anti-dissociation camp first. The anti-dissociatives. Come.
Gotō: being awake is always better than dissociating.
